chunks: Those who wait to see what befalls you, say in ease success comes to you from God: 'Were we not with you?' But if fortune favours the infidels, they say: 'Did we not overpower you, and yet protected you against the believers?' But God will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection; and God will never give the unbelievers a way over the faithful.
ai.seo_question: How did the hypocrites justify their presence with the Muslims in battle?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the opportunistic nature of the hypocrites (al-munafiqun) who remained in Medina, waiting to see which side would prevail in battles like Badr or Uhud. Their dual claim-making illustrates the concept of 'waiting for the outcome' (tarabbus), and the conclusion emphasizes that God will prevent the disbelievers from gaining lasting authority over the faithful, a theme central to the struggle between truth and falsehood.
